title: Targeting papillomavirus infections: high-throughput screening reveals an effective inhibitor of cutaneous beta-HPV types.
authors: Ibragimov, Ruslan; Babok, Sofiya; Lototskaja-Perepelenko, Elina; Ivanova, Larisa; Mikhailava, Nika; Zaikina, Lidiia; Piirsoo, Marko; Piirsoo, Alla
one_liner_zh: 高通量筛选发现NSC51349抑制皮肤HPV5复制，机制涉及E2蛋白转录活性抑制及分子对接预测结合位点，但核心是抗病毒药物筛选，非TF-DNA互作建模，仅分子对接部分与课题弱相关。
abstract: Cutaneous and mucosal human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are implicated in the development of various cancers. To date, there are no HPV-specific antivirals, and vaccines designed for mucosal HPV types are ineffective against cutaneous HPV variants and ongoing infections. These facts, along with the increasing prevalence of specific types of HPV-positive cancers, underscore the unmet need for HPV antiviral drugs. In this study, we performed a high-throughput screening using the National Cancer Institute Diversity Set VI library of small-molecule compounds and identified 5,7-dimethoxy-2-pyridin-3-ylchromen-4-one (NSC51349) as a potent inhibitor of oncogenic cutaneous HPV5 replication in U2OS cells. Further analysis showed that NSC51349 specifically inhibits replication of the HPV5 genome in human primary keratinocytes (IC50  approximately  4 microM) without detrimental effects on cell cycle, viability, or differentiation. In addition, this compound efficiently inhibits replication of the other cutaneous HPV types 8 and 38, and Macaca fascicularis PV type 1 genomes. The mechanism of NSC51349-mediated inhibition involves the suppression of the viral protein E2 transcriptional activity. Molecular docking predicted that NSC51349 interacts with the HPV5 E2 protein by binding to the threonine 202/proline 203 and threonine 473/glutamate 474 amino acid residues, located at the junction of the transactivation domain and hinge region, and the DNA-binding domain, respectively. Our study suggests that NSC51349 is a promising lead compound for further development of cutaneous HPV antiviral drugs.IMPORTANCEHuman papillomaviruses (HPVs) are linked to various cancers of the skin and mucous membranes. While vaccines exist for some mucosal HPV types, they are ineffective against skin-infecting variants and cannot treat existing infections. This highlights the urgent need for HPV-specific antiviral drugs. In this study, we identified a promising lead compound, 5,7-dimethoxy-2-pyridin-3-ylchromen-4-one (NSC51349), through high-throughput screening of the Diversity Set VI library of small molecules. NSC51349 inhibits the replication of HPV5, a cancer-associated skin virus, in human cells without affecting cell viability, growth, or differentiation. It also inhibits the replication of other cutaneous HPV types, including HPV8 and HPV38, further supporting its broad potential. NSC51349 targets the viral protein E2, which is crucial for HPV replication. By binding to specific regions of E2, it interferes with its transcriptional activity, halting viral replication and the expression of viral oncogenes. This study introduces NSC51349 as a strong candidate for antiviral drug development.
abstract_zh: 皮肤和黏膜人乳头瘤病毒（HPVs）与多种癌症的发生有关。迄今为止，尚无针对HPV的特异性抗病毒药物，且针对黏膜型HPV设计的疫苗对皮肤型HPV变异株及持续感染无效。这些事实，加上特定类型HPV阳性癌症患病率的不断上升，凸显了HPV抗病毒药物的未满足需求。在本研究中，我们利用国家癌症研究所多样性集VI小分子化合物库进行了高通量筛选，并鉴定出5,7-二甲氧基-2-吡啶-3-基色烯-4-酮（NSC51349）作为U2OS细胞中致癌性皮肤型HPV5复制的强效抑制剂。进一步分析表明，NSC51349特异性抑制人原代角质形成细胞中HPV5基因组的复制（IC50 约 4微摩尔），且对细胞周期、活力或分化无不良影响。此外，该化合物有效抑制其他皮肤型HPV类型8和38，以及食蟹猴乳头瘤病毒1型基因组的复制。NSC51349介导抑制的机制涉及病毒蛋白E2转录活性的抑制。分子对接预测NSC51349通过与HPV5 E2蛋白的苏氨酸202/脯氨酸203和苏氨酸473/谷氨酸474氨基酸残基结合相互作用，这些残基分别位于反式激活结构域与铰链区交界处，以及DNA结合结构域。我们的研究表明，NSC51349是进一步开发皮肤型HPV抗病毒药物的有前景的先导化合物。重要性 人乳头瘤病毒（HPVs）与皮肤和黏膜的多种癌症相关。虽然存在针对某些黏膜型HPV的疫苗，但它们对感染皮肤的变异株无效，且无法治疗现有感染。这凸显了对HPV特异性抗病毒药物的迫切需求。在本研究中，我们通过对多样性集VI小分子库的高通量筛选，鉴定出一个有前景的先导化合物5,7-二甲氧基-2-吡啶-3-基色烯-4-酮（NSC51349）。NSC51349抑制HPV5（一种与癌症相关的皮肤病毒）在人细胞中的复制，且不影响细胞活力、生长或分化。它还抑制其他皮肤型HPV类型（包括HPV8和HPV38）的复制，进一步支持其广泛潜力。NSC51349靶向病毒蛋白E2，该蛋白对HPV复制至关重要。通过结合E2的特定区域，它干扰其转录活性，从而阻止病毒复制和病毒癌基因的表达。本研究将NSC51349作为抗病毒药物开发的强候选物引入。
